q: Which EU accreditation bodies accept CBAM verifiers based outside the EU?
title: EU bodies accrediting non-EU CBAM verifiers
short: As of the Commission's 21 October 2026 update, seven of the 24 national accreditation bodies offering CBAM accreditation accept verifiers based outside the EU: COFRAC (France), ESYD (Greece), Accredia (Italy), RvA (Netherlands), PCA (Poland), SNAS (Slovakia) and Swedac (Sweden). An Indian verifier's CBAM certificate should come from one of them.
audience: Indian plant owners choosing a CBAM verifier, and Indian verification firms seeking accreditation

sections.h: Why only an EU body counts
p: CBAM accreditation can only be granted by a national accreditation body in an EU Member State, or in an EEA country once CBAM is part of the EEA Agreement. An accreditation from an Indian or other non-EU body does not make a firm a CBAM verifier. It can only shorten the EU assessment, as evidence of competence in ISO 17029 or ISO 14065. So an accreditation from NABCB in India, or an accreditation as a verification agency under India's carbon market (CCTS), does not let a firm sign CBAM reports. What the Commission's guidance names is an existing ISO 17029 or ISO 14065 accreditation, from an EU or non-EU body: the EU body must take it into account and can simplify the assessment. It says nothing specific about CCTS accreditation, so treat that as background, not a shortcut.

sections.h: The seven that take third-country applicants
ul: Netherlands: Raad voor Accreditatie (RvA). The Commission's table also notes an agreement with Turkey's TURKAK.
Sweden: Swedac. The table notes agreements with Ukraine's NAAU and the UK's UKAS.

sections.h: Bodies that do not take non-EU firms
p: The other national bodies offering CBAM accreditation, including Germany's DAkkS, Austria's AA, Belgium's BELAC, Finland's FINAS and Spain's ENAC, had not agreed to accredit third-country applicants as of 21 October 2026. Some, such as the Czech, Hungarian and Romanian bodies, were not yet ready to accept any applications. Cyprus, Estonia, Ireland and Malta do not offer CBAM accreditation at all. The table changes, so check the dated Commission file before relying on it.

sections.h: If you run an Indian verification firm
ul: You may choose any EU body that offers the service, but apply to one only. Bodies share application lists to weed out duplicates.
State your scopes, such as cement, crude steel or aluminium products, in the application. You need not cover every sector.
Expect a document review, an office audit and at least one witness audit at a real installation. A new accreditation normally takes 6 to 12 months.
You may sign a verification contract and start preliminary work before accreditation, but you can issue the verification report only once accredited and registered in the CBAM Registry.

The certificate lasts at most five years, with surveillance every year, the first within 12 months. The accreditation body can reduce your scope, suspend you, during which you may not verify, or withdraw the accreditation.

sections.h: If you run an Indian plant
ol: Ask the verifier for its CBAM accreditation certificate and check the issuing body against the seven above, or against an EU firm's own national body.
Check that the scope on the certificate covers your goods.

Check that the accreditation is valid, and not suspended, on the day the verification report will be issued, not only when you sign. Your customers' verifiers check the same when they rely on your report for a precursor.
Check the verifier is registered in the CBAM Registry. The Commission will publish the list of accredited verifiers on its CBAM verification page.

senseible: Senseible's CBAM Suite exports a verifier pack with an evidence index, a sampling list and a checklist, which any accredited verifier you appoint can work from. Senseible does not accredit verifiers and is not an accredited CBAM verifier.
